title: DAANVEER: Ministry of Panchayati Raj Calls for Public Participation to Strengthen Digital Infrastructure in Gram Panchayats
subtitle: Simple, Secure and Transparent Digital Process Enables Computer Donations Directly to Any Eligible Gram Panchayat through Meri Panchayat App
body_text:
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj invites public participation to become ‘DAANVEERs’ and contribute towards strengthening digital infrastructure at the grassroots. DAANVEER , a people-led Computer Crowdsourcing Initiative, enables individuals and organizations to donate desktop computers directly to verified Gram Panchayats through a simple, transparent and technology-enabled mechanism. Complementing infrastructure support provided under Government programs, including the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), the initiative seeks to harness voluntary public participation to strengthen digital governance and service delivery at the grassroots.
DAANVEER makes donating a computer to a Gram Panchayat as simple and convenient as an online purchase. Through the Meri Panchayat App, citizens can view Gram Panchayats verified by the respective State Governments requiring desktop computers and choose to support their own or any other eligible Gram Panchayat, all from their phone. On clicking “Donate Computer”, the donor is securely redirected to DigiHaat, an ONDC-enabled digital marketplace, without the need for separate registration. The selected Panchayat’s delivery address and recipient details are automatically populated, eliminating manual data entry. Donors can choose from standardized computer bundles aligned with prescribed technical specifications, make the payment digitally and track the order from confirmation and dispatch to delivery and acknowledgement. Following acknowledgement by the Gram Panchayat Secretary, the donor receives a digitally generated Certificate of Appreciation. Hence under the initiative, every stage of the donation journey, from order placement to delivery, can be tracked in real time, ensuring complete transparency.
A computer donated through DAANVEER can strengthen a Gram Panchayat’s capacity to effectively use digital governance platforms for planning, financial management, record-keeping and citizen service delivery. The initiative combines this impact with a transparent donation process, enabling public to view the donation status of their Gram Panchayat and donors to digitally track their contribution. It also offers citizens living away from their native villages, including the Indian diaspora, philanthropic organizations and CSR partners, a credible avenue to contribute to grassroots digital infrastructure and reconnect with their villages. With more States onboarding eligible Gram Panchayats, DAANVEER has the potential to evolve into a nationwide movement for stronger and digitally empowered Panchayats. As on 27 th August 2026, 75 donations have already been made, marking an enthusiastic response and growing public acceptance of this initiative. On successful completion, donors receive a Certificate of Appreciation, recognizing their contribution to strengthening local governance. DAANVEER represents an innovative model of participatory governance, enabling voluntary public participation to complement Government efforts in strengthening grassroots institutions. Citizens, philanthropists, organizations, CSR partners and members of the Indian diaspora are encouraged to come forward and become a DAANVEER.
Scan the QR code, register on the Meri Panchayat App. For more details, visit: https://egramswaraj.gov.in/danveer/

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has launched 'DAANVEER', a crowdsourcing initiative allowing citizens, NGOs, CSR partners and the diaspora to donate desktop computers directly to verified Gram Panchayats via the Meri Panchayat App. Donors are redirected to the ONDC-enabled DigiHaat marketplace where Panchayat delivery details are auto-populated, payment is made digitally, and the donation is tracked end-to-end, with a digital Certificate of Appreciation issued after acknowledgement. As of 27 August 2026, 75 donations have been made under the initiative, which complements infrastructure support under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA).
enrichment.context:
Digital governance at the grassroots has been a priority area under RGSA, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj's flagship scheme aimed at strengthening Panchayati Raj Institutions' capacity for planning, financial management, and service delivery through platforms like eGramSwaraj and the Meri Panchayat App. Many Gram Panchayats still lack adequate computer hardware, limiting their ability to use e-governance tools effectively despite growing digitisation mandates.

DAANVEER represents a public-private-citizen participation model that leverages the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) infrastructure to enable a transparent, trackable donation mechanism, distinguishing it from traditional CSR or philanthropic routes that often lack accountability. It also creates an avenue for the Indian diaspora and citizens who have migrated from villages to contribute to their native Panchayats, aligning with the broader push for participatory and cooperative governance at the local level.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'DAANVEER' initiative launched by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj:
1. It enables individuals to donate desktop computers to Gram Panchayats through the Meri Panchayat App.
2. The donation payment is processed through the ONDC-enabled DigiHaat marketplace.
3. It replaces the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) as the primary scheme for digital infrastructure in Panchayats.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: DAANVEER uses the Meri Panchayat App and DigiHaat (ONDC-enabled) for computer donations to Gram Panchayats, and it complements—not replaces—RGSA, which continues to provide infrastructure support.

prelims_questions.question: 'ONDC', referred to in the context of the DAANVEER initiative, stands for:
options: Organised Network for Development and Commerce
prelims_questions.explanation: ONDC stands for Open Network for Digital Commerce, an open e-commerce protocol used here to facilitate transparent computer donations to Gram Panchayats via DigiHaat.

mains_questions.question: Examine how citizen-led crowdsourcing initiatives like DAANVEER can complement government schemes such as the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan in strengthening digital governance at the grassroots level.
Discuss the significance of digital infrastructure in enhancing the functioning of Panchayati Raj Institutions and the challenges in achieving last-mile digital governance in rural India.
